# FEVER OF UNKNOWN ORIGIN

Fever of unknown origin (FUO) is the occurrence of several episodes of fever greater than 101 degrees Fahrenheit over a period of at least 3 weeks despite 1 week of hospital evaluation. Empirical antimicrobial therapy is rarely indicated except in patients who are neutropenic, immunocompromised, or critically ill.
For prolonged fever in neutropenic patients refer to the neutropenic fever recommendations.

[Neutropenic fever](immunocom-neut-fever)
